```{r doc-code, include=FALSE}
source("../code/R/doc_code.R")
```

All panels are produced by
[`script/Figure4.R`](https://github.com/dzemmour/immgenT-cosmo-paper/blob/main/script/Figure4.R).
The code below is shown for reference (not re-executed on this page); the
images are its pre-rendered output.

Panels **d-g** and **h-j** are two matched sets of views of the same tissue and
cell type, with and without an immune challenge: a small-intestine lamina
propria sample 30 days after LCMV Armstrong infection, and one from a naive
mouse.

## Setup

```{r fig4-setup, code=code_for("../script/Figure4.R", c("^", "Load data")), eval=FALSE}
```

## (A) Saturation of cluster discovery {#fig4a}

```{r fig4a-code, code=code_for("../script/Figure4.R", "4a"), eval=FALSE}
```

```{r fig4a-img, echo=FALSE, out.width="70%"}
knitr::include_graphics("assets/Figure4/4a_saturation_clusters.png")
```

::: {.figcaption}
**Fig. 4A.** Saturation of T-cell states within the immgenT dataset. A cluster
counts as discovered at the experiment where its cumulative cell total first
exceeds 50. The number of such clusters reaches saturation after the 69th
experiment; the dashed line marks the final count of 107.
:::

## (B) Silhouette width before vs. after integration {#fig4b}

```{r fig4b-code, code=code_for("../script/Figure4.R", "4b"), eval=FALSE}
```

```{r fig4b-img, echo=FALSE, out.width="45%"}
knitr::include_graphics("assets/Figure4/4b_silhouette_pre_post_integration.png")
```

::: {.figcaption}
**Fig. 4B.** Cluster separation (mean silhouette width) before integration
(within each dataset, on its own principal components) and after integration
into the immgenT latent space, showing the extent to which well-separated
clusters remain distinct following integration. Clusters here are defined de
novo within each experiment, independently of the atlas annotation. Colours
indicate experiment (IGT). Scores > 0 denote well-separated clusters.
R² = 0.38.
:::

## (C) Cluster separability in RNA space {#fig4c}

```{r fig4c-code, code=code_for("../script/Figure4.R", "4c"), eval=FALSE}
```

```{r fig4c-img, echo=FALSE, out.width="100%"}
knitr::include_graphics("assets/Figure4/4c_cluster_separability_RNA.png")
```

::: {.figcaption}
**Fig. 4C.** Distribution of cluster separability scores (see Methods) for each
immgenT consensus cluster across experiments, in gene expression space. Scores
> 0 indicate transcriptionally distinct clusters; across 3,511 cluster-by-
experiment combinations with at least 10 cells, 99.5% are positive. Colours
indicate experiment (IGT). Proliferative clusters score lowest, consistent with
cells from multiple lineages entering the cell cycle.
:::

## (D) One sample's composition against all samples {#fig4d}

```{r fig4d-code, code=code_for("../script/Figure4.R", "4d"), eval=FALSE}
```

```{r fig4d-img, echo=FALSE, out.width="100%"}
knitr::include_graphics("assets/Figure4/4d_sample_composition_I40H8.png")
```

::: {.figcaption}
**Fig. 4D.** Proportion of each immgenT cluster within each lineage in the
LCMV sample. Background boxplots show the distribution of cluster proportions
across all samples in the atlas, highlighting clusters enriched in this sample:
most of its CD8 T cells map to CD8.Q.
:::

## (E, H) Sample CD8 cells on the CD8 MDE {#fig4eh}

```{r fig4eh-code, code=code_for("../script/Figure4.R", "4e/4h"), eval=FALSE}
```

```{r fig4eh-img, echo=FALSE, out.width="45%"}
knitr::include_graphics(c("assets/Figure4/4e_CD8MDE_I40H8.png",
                          "assets/Figure4/4h_CD8MDE_I21H9.png"))
```

::: {.figcaption}
**Fig. 4E, H.** Each sample's CD8 T cells on the CD8-specific MDE, with all
immgenT CD8 T cells shown in grey for reference. **E**: 30 days after LCMV
Armstrong infection. **H**: naive mouse — CD8.Q cells are rare at baseline.
:::

## (F, I) Experiment-specific UMAP {#fig4fi}

```{r fig4fi-code, code=code_for("../script/Figure4.R", "4f/4i"), eval=FALSE}
```

```{r fig4fi-img, echo=FALSE, out.width="40%"}
knitr::include_graphics(c("assets/Figure4/4f_IGT40_UMAP_CD8Q.png",
                          "assets/Figure4/4i_IGT21_UMAP_CD8Q.png"))
```

::: {.figcaption}
**Fig. 4F, I.** Each sample re-embedded on its own, as it would be analysed
without the atlas, with the cells the atlas assigns to CD8.Q highlighted in
green. **F**: in the infected sample they cluster together. **I**: in the naive
sample the rare CD8.Q cells do not form a distinct cluster.
:::

## (G, J) CD8.Q cells in protein space {#fig4gj}

```{r fig4gj-code, code=code_for("../script/Figure4.R", "4g/4j"), eval=FALSE}
```

```{r fig4gj-img, echo=FALSE, out.width="40%"}
knitr::include_graphics(c("assets/Figure4/4g_IGT40_CD8Q_CD103_ITGB7.png",
                          "assets/Figure4/4j_IGT21_CD8Q_CD103_ITGB7.png"))
```

::: {.figcaption}
**Fig. 4G, J.** Each sample's CD8.Q cells express the tissue-resident memory
markers CD103 and ITGB7 (CITE-seq, log1p(CP10K)); all other CD8 T cells from
that experiment are shown in grey. The reference assignment was made from the
transcriptome alone and predicts a protein phenotype it was not given, in both
the infected (**G**) and the naive (**J**) sample.
:::
